subject.title: feat: AI safety event taxonomy — core event contracts

question: Should AI-safety events remain a core-internal trusted contract with only a manifest-gated plugin emission API, or should ordinary plugins be allowed to call a public trusted emitter for these events?
rationale: The answer defines both the permanent Plugin SDK compatibility contract and whether third-party code can assert operator-facing safety findings with trusted provenance; implementation mechanics cannot safely choose that policy.

options.title: Core-internal trust boundary
options.body: Keep AI-safety payloads out of the public trusted emitter and permit plugin emissions only through the manifest-gated API with untrusted provenance.

options.title: Public trusted plugin contract
options.body: Intentionally expose trusted safety-event emission to plugins, document which plugins qualify as trusted, and add authorization, provenance, compatibility, and abuse tests.

options.title: Pause the taxonomy series
options.body: Do not merge the event contracts until the taxonomy, privacy/cardinality rules, and long-term versioning model have a maintainer-sponsored design.

recommendation.title: Core-internal trust boundary
recommendation.body: Keep AI-safety payloads out of the public trusted emitter and permit plugin emissions only through the manifest-gated API with untrusted provenance.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans public Plugin SDK compatibility, operator-visible security provenance, and core product direction.
